facts.text: Gift certificates cannot expire or have fees within 4 years after purchase.
facts.quote: A person may not sell or issue a gift certificate that, within 4 years after the date of purchase, is subject to expiration or a fee or charge of any kind.

facts.text: Any expiration or fee terms effective after 4 years must be clearly printed in at least 10 point type on the gift certificate or its packaging.
facts.quote: Any term or condition concerning expiration or a fee or charge that takes effect more than 4 years after the date of purchase must be printed clearly in at least 10 point type in a visible place on: (1) The front or back of the gift certificate; (2) A sticker permanently affixed to the gift certificate; or (3) An envelope containing the gift certificate.

facts.text: Terms about expiration or fees cannot be changed after purchase unless the change benefits the consumer.
facts.quote: Unless the change benefits the consumer, a term or condition disclosed under subsection (c) of this section may not be changed after the date of purchase or issuance.

facts.text: Gift certificates sold or issued in violation of these rules are still valid and cannot expire or have fees.
facts.quote: A gift certificate that is sold or issued in violation of this section shall be considered valid and may not be subject to expiration or any fee or charge.
